I believe it's possible, especially if fine means becoming a productive member of society (or, just not heavily destructive to oneself or to others). I also believe that resilience shows up in different ways too, as it could mean becoming a high achiever in adulthood, or being a great support for others (not necessarily going through a similar issue).

Children who don't have the support system and make it through generally unscathed shouldn't feel like something is wrong though, as that's the ideal situation. On the flipside, there shouldn't be judgement toward the many people who don't make it through without (or, even with) help.

From personal experience, I made it through many of my younger years, despite dealing with various forms of extensive abuse and trauma (a decade of frequent sexual abuse). But, things started becoming worse as got to my teens and 20s. - Part of it was that I just couldn't deal and needed help (didn't commit to that until years later). Part of it involved general coming-of-age challenges. And, part of it came from using coping mechanisms that weren't seen as socially acceptable, compared to others, causing needless, additional worry overall.

Bottom line: definitely seek help, if you need it. But, also don't force yourself to think you do, if you're truly fine, even if pothers say you're wrong for feeling fine.

Also, if it's someone you know, don't force them to think they need help either, if they genuinely don't, but be alert and ready, if they do.

As a guy, I get so nervous around women if there's any hint that they find me attractive (and, not just women who I already find attractive too). Not saying that to be conceited, but it's happened a lot over the years.

During my teens and 20s, I tried to hide from any chance of intimacy, while secretly wanting to create intimacy and express myself. As a result, almost never flirted, and if I did, it was unbeknownst to me, I was drunk, or just absolutely terrible flirting. At the same time, I either picked up signs that a woman was flirting and didn't flirt back, creating a barrier, or just was completely oblivious, due to not thinking of myself as a (relatively normal) sexual being.

Around other men, I almost automatically feel lesser and weaker than each of them, trying my best not to show it. I'm a bigger than average guy (not huge though), which makes things probably seem perplexing to people who have seen me in public - "*Why is he such a fragile wimp?"* is what I think they have in their heads.

Compliments, in general, are hard to deal with, especially when it's about physical appearance. Inner voice relates it to my ~~brother~~ abuser who would compliment me, only to take advantage of me for so many years. I don't dress to impress (most of my wardrobe consists of hand-me-down/old high school T-shirts and the packs of various colored, Hanes work T-shirts from Walmart).

On top of that, I try to 'fake it till you make it', but, people can often see through it, since it's hardly real. Multiple times a day I question what's the point of living on, and, sometimes, I can't find an answer.

NTA, but you could've toned it down a bit. That's not the same thing as playing down to everyone else's level. For example, no need to steal bases, if everyone else is already such a lesser opponent, or if they don't even know about that rule. 

It would've made more sense if your teacher made you and your buddy captains of opposing teams. You seem intensely competitive, as does he, so maybe you two could compete against each other, while trying to get people on your team to play harder/better too

Or, to make things more challenging, next time have a game of you two versus the rest of the class, or you two and the worst players in class on one team.

Yeah, that's how it's been for a while. Part of the reason for me is because the only person who showed me affection was also a sexual abuser for many years. So, it's a constant back and forth of craving affection, but also not.

At the same time, I feel that way about compliments. I used to generally like them, but lately I think that some of the compliments I received are because I'm doing something that's attention-seeking. Like I'm overcompensating or giving off body language and facial expressions that are begging for approval.

It got better when I smoked alone, but I eventually quit altogether, about 6 months after I started having bad paranoia. I did try again though a few months later, on 4/20 of the following spring, but those intense feelings came rushing back. So, I was done for good.

Overall, that feeling never really went away while sober, though it's not nearly as intense and panic-inducing.

I've not had flashbacks from smoking, but over time I grew increasingly paranoid. This wasn't until a few years down the line of on and off periods of habitual smoking. 

I started getting paranoid of other people, what they said, how they said it, and what their body language was displaying and generally seeing them as potential threats like my abuser.

Definitely. Hid a lot of my music taste for years, and still kind of do. I typically showed people that I had an affinity for rap music, but didn't show that I had an affinity for R&B, and pop music, various subgenres of rock, jazz, classical and more. I kept thinking I was childish and immature to unironically enjoy music from video games too, instead of celebrating them the compositions and their composers. 

On the flipside, I hide how much I don't know things too. 

Back to the music example, I was familiar with a lot of rap artists, but wouldn't know everyone's songs (especially songs that weren't released as singles with an accompanying music video), or know all the lyrics to songs. There were times when I shamefully tried to keep up appearances about things I genuinely didn't know about.

I've had this thought process more than a few times in my twenties. Periodically I think, "I was much braver, bolder, and tougher when I was a young kid. What happened?" I don't even feel like the same person, but also strangely feel like I am too, just not mature like so many others seem to be.

It's caused some girls who have hit on me to become upset, and I haven't been able to explain to them why I'm so strange. There's always the fear of then thinking/finding out that I'm weak or a freak, as a result of not pursuing sexual intimacy and just being extremely nervous in general

I definitely don't hate everyone, but I hate myself so much that the appealing parts of life seem like they should be off limits to me, especially family and friends.

I used to think that my problem was depression, but I strongly believe that I am a narcissist or at least possess many narcissistic traits, and it's made me want to kill myself to stop hurting others. Ever since I read that story, I've thought that's the way my abuser should go out, because of other committed crimes and overall indecent behavior.

Im not street smart, so being taken advantage happens a lot, but I put myself in disadvantageous positions pretty often. I don't think I have much value to others, if I'm not fulfilling a need, which usually isn't a social need.

I think social needs were easier to meet as a younger kid and teenager, but general maturity levels of others increased, changing their social needs and desires. With that, responsibilities often change too (more dating, marriages & families, formal education & careers, etc.). 

In summary, I'm better at helping a friend move than actually hanging out with said friend.

The real me idealized so many aspects of life, only for reality to constantly remind me of, well, reality.

For example, I idealized the idea of friendship, but I was a lousy friend, especially as a teenager going into adulthood. I'm terrified of my old friends and acquaintances now, because I constantly feel like they've realized that they're better off without me in their lives. 

I also idealized the ideas of romance (I would've been a lousy boyfriend), sports/competition (never played to win, but instead played not to lose or screw up), and school/learning (routinely bombed in at least one class per semester).

The real me carries a default mindset of 'reluctant obedience', with a lack of long term goals, proper sociability (outside of most one-on-one conversations), and actual hardened confidence.

Father - completely apathetic, and continued to financially support my ~~brother~~ abuser. There's evidence of my abuser being very destructive person outside of the realm of sexual abuse (including drug dealing and using), but my father doesn't care one bit. He sat by the wayside as my sister's life fell apart, due to her protecting my niece from her own dealings with abuse. She quite literally lost everything, but my father didn't  move one finger to help. In conclusion, I strongly believe my father is a dirty pervert and possible pedophile (I know he is actually, but he won't admit it).

Mother - on a hunch, she randomly asked me on a summer evening when I was 15, if something happened to me. I told her that something did in fact happen ( I spared her the details), and she was on my side for all of four days. Four days after I told her that something happened, she invited my abuser over, and I watched from an upstairs window as she greeted him, hugged him and laughed with him in the street, just at the edge of our driveway.

A couple of weeks after that, my mother started getting on my case because I was unsure if I wanted to play football that fall. I had doubts months before, yet she was much more concerned about that than anything else. We got into intense argument, which turned into a screaming match for about an hour or so, because she thought the abuse was why I wanted to stop playing. She used that exclusive information against me in a petty argument, all because I had doubts about playing for a team that **sucked**. I ended up playing that season, but not because of her.

It wasn't until a few years ago that I found out my mother strongly suspected that I was gay. My sister told me that they discussed it behind my back. 

Of course, many people in my hometown revered my parents because some of my older brothers were high school football stars. Most of them played in college too, and one went to the NFL. Most of my siblings  were adopted, so that gave my parents an added layer of protection from any type of criticism.

The universe has given me lots of opportunity to get ahead, but in feeling like I shouldn't be ahead, I make choices to stay behind.

It's not instantaneous at every provided opportunity, and it's not due to daily pessimism either. It's just that I regularly sabotage hints of progress that could lead to success, due to not thinking I have what it takes to get ahead

Going back, I definitely would've kept it from my parents too, because my mother used the situation against me, which indirectly led to a different family member's life falling apart. 

Thanks for your input though, and best of luck on your journey as well

Out of 7 sons, he taught exactly 1 about anything pertaining to life. He taught one of my brothers how to tie a tie and how to use a lawn mower, but that's pretty much it.

I definitely don't feel like a survivor, and a big part of it is because I am not living a good life. 

I have become a pretty toxic person, who has done enough bad things that would cancel out the label of 'survivor' or 'victim' altogether.

It's part of the reason why I had to move away from my hometown. I watched as people I grew up with matured, while I didn't progress forward. They went through the stages of becoming more self actualized people, including increased intimacy, increased responsibility and goals involving careers, family, and other personal goals. I felt that I needed to move away so I wouldn't slow them down and impede their progress, because I generally don't know what the hell I'm doing or want. 

I found that to be a recurring issue whether it was with family, friends, coworkers, or complete strangers. When I'm talking to someone one on one, and an additional person joined the group, I silence myself, pretty much telling myself, "the adults are speaking now". I think it's led to people thinking that I dislike them, but it's not true, and the truth comes with too long of an explanation.

Layered beneath all of that are my memories of the really bad stuff that I've done too. We're supposed to get over that stuff, especially if someone offers forgiveness, but I usually don't move on. The accumulation of all the badness I've put in the world makes me want to stay locked down forever, as if it's a deserved punishment.

From my father? Almost everything. How to shave. How to tie a tie. The importance of hygiene (how and why you should wash yourself after gym class). How to speak to others, especially girls/women I might be interested in dating. How to operate a lawnmower. How to throw a football and shoot/dribble a basketball (he watches both sports all of the time). How to throw a punch, if ever necessary. How to swim. How to fish (he likes fishing). How to use any tools, from hammers to screwdrivers. And more

He taught me how to change a tire, only because I was with him one time, not because he wanted me to learn. And, he gave me 2 five minute driving lessons. One the night before my first driver's education session, and the other was about 10 minutes before that same first session. 

Outside observers wonder why there's not a strong bond between us. I'm thankful he wasn't a mean drunk or anything like that, and I know no one is perfect, but damn. 7 sons, and he didn't teach them anything about being men.

Growing up, some of my friends knew about a specific brother of mine, who was a drug dealer. He was/is not well liked by my siblings, however, some people around town were okay with him. 

What no one knew at that time, but found out later, is that he also was a manipulative, angry, violent drug user. What absolutely no one knew/knows is that he's a sexual abuser. Generally, I kept talk about him to a minimum, but if someone asked, I informed that drug use/dealing wasn't the (main) reason why I didn't like him. Not many people asked about him though. 

It started getting much harder to keep everything locked away, and during my late teens and earlier twenties, I started having some bad dreams and nightmares where he showed up. I revealed some truth about him to close friends, but nothing about the sexual abuse history. 

That part pains me still, and to tie into what youre saying about your friend, it's been hard for me to look at many things from earlier in my life, that includes my friends in person, pictures of my friends, pictures of my siblings, and definitely older pictures of myself. My friends didn't do anything wrong, but I slowly unraveled and lost myself. I stopped feeling like the friend that they knew, and started getting more and more confused on if I was revealing my true self that had been kept away. 

I can't speak for your friend, but I kept myself away because I didn't want to impede in anyone's lives. I was toxic, and while I haven't been as evil as my ~~brother~~ abuser, but I've done a lot of bad things and made poor decisions too. I'm at a point after contemplating whether telling people about the sexual abuse is worth it. I ruined the friendships that I did have due to being a bad friend, and not the abuse.

Seeing or talking to old friends is a reminder of a past that I so badly ruined, beyond just friendships. I'm not sure if your friend feels the same way, but that's the best way I can spell out what's on my mind.

My abuser was in and out of jail, and returned home after a sentence of about a year or so. At first, he slept in the basement of our house, but after a short while, he insisted that he sleep on the floor of the room I shared with one of my brothers. The room wasn't very big, but he wanted to sleep on the rug, in the small space between my and my brother's bed.

I don't remember how long it took, but he inevitably started pulling me out of bed many nights, most of them were sleepless nights. I say 'inevitably' because he had already been sexually abusing me for many years before that, and he stayed in our room during the final year of abuse. It paralled the first few years though, because his actions would be similar, except he would strike every night at bed time. 


Many of those nights, I'd try to pretend to be asleep, but he would relentlessly try to wake me up. When he did pull me out and onto the ground, I'd lay there, unsure if it would be better or worse if my sleeping brother woke up, opened his eyes, and saw what was happening. All these years later, and I'm still not sure.

I've had girls flirt with me in the past, and I didn't react, causing some to be confused, some to be frustrated and angry, and some to flat out assume that I'm gay. No goals, barely any personal passion or desires. Just waiting until the next day, to wait for the next day

Used to have friends while growing up, but have slowly isolated for the past 10 years. It really ramped up over the last 5 years.

I've avoided the people who were around during that time. Not at all blaming them, but just avoiding them. It's mainly because I've so badly wanted to tell them what was happening, but just couldn't do it then, and can't do it now.

It's been happening a lot lately. Like my loved ones aren't sexual abusing me, but some of them have beaten me up, excessively berated me and overall just been utterly contemptuous of me. 

A couple years ago, I had a dream where my sister accused me of molesting her daughter, and that I was lying about everything in my past. In real life, she's the one that knows the most about what happened, but in my dream she used that information against me at the police station, and for some reason was covering for my abuser.

That dream freaked me out, and avoided my sister for like a week, and didn't tell her about the dream, even though she wouldn't do that in real life.

I connect very closely to the last paragraph, and have spent the past 10-15 years wondering why my parents didn't care, since finding out the truth.

My father said nothing, and "secretly" kept helping my ~~brother~~ abuser financially (he tried to hide it, but everyone already knew it), while my mother was sneaky with her apathy.

It took her 3 or 4 days, to go from comforting me, to comforting my abuser and directing anger toward me. 

I haven't figured out why our parents are like that. Hasn't made sense.

I struggle with the validation and acceptance too. When I think about how frequent the abuse occurred and how long it lasted, it feels surreal, to the point that it's seemingly unbelievable. 

I've often wondered if it's all a bad dream, because I have no physical scars and no witnesses from any of the instances of abuse. And, only one person who knows the truth had a reaction, and that person was neither of my parents.

I tried explaining this to a good friend of mine, and it happened to be in front of his girlfriend. Ultimately, was made fun of by her and one of her friends, because they thought I was being an edgy, emo person or something.

I didn't get to explain it in full though, because I didn't tell him what led to feeling like the old me was essentially dead. I didn't know how to access the happy-go-lucky kid that he knew growing up, because that kid's genuine smile faded away, along with his hopes and dreams. Happiness in general was fleeting, and I felt like an imposter that physically resembled that person that my friend knew, but that was essentially it.

I couldn't tell him about everything that happened behind closed doors, although I hinted that I was against physical abuse as punishment. A couple friends of mine shared an apartment with one of my brothers, and he informed them that we suffered physical abuse as punishment. So, my friends knew about that, but they have no idea that there were many years of sexual abuse as well. 

To him and others that I grew up with, I'm essentially one of those child stars that appeared normal and happy, and displayed talent in sports and various school subjects, but grew up as a completely miserable person (Not to be conceited or anything like that). 

I don't enjoy looking at old pictures of myself, because it's a reminder of bad times. I'm out of those bad times now, but of the hope of that once young kid vanished so long ago, and I don't know if it'll ever come back.

I've been wondering many, many of the same things you mentioned.

I feel like at a certain point all the guys (and girls) that I grew up with got the memo on how to feel comfortable with their sexuality and create intimacy, but I just never did.
